cases.input: An internal need with scope, quantity, owner and budget reference is approved.
cases.expect: The request may initiate sourcing but creates no supplier, contract or order fact.

cases.input: One approved request is fulfilled through two independently issued orders.
cases.expect: The request retains one identity and references both orders without merging them.

cases.input: A request is withdrawn after review but before sourcing.
cases.expect: Its revisions and approval history remain resolvable.

cases.input: Internal request approval is treated as supplier award.
A budget reference is treated as committed and available funding.
The approved request is issued to a supplier as a purchase order.
Requested quantity changes after approval; a new revision is created with revisionEffectiveFrom and supersedesRevisionRef.
cases.expect: Both revisions remain resolvable and the prior approval stays pinned to the scope revision it authorized.

cases.input: A scope revision is recorded by setting replacementRequestRef to a new request identifier instead of creating a revision.
cases.expect: Rejected: revision succession and distinct-need replacement are separate fields with separate meanings.

cases.input: A request reaches status 'approved' with no approvals entry and no authorityRef.
cases.expect: Rejected: approval requires an approver, authority binding, decision instant and the approved scope revision.

cases.input: One approved request is fulfilled by two independently issued purchase orders.
cases.expect: orderRefs holds both order references under one request identity; the orders are not merged and no contract is implied.

cases.input: The request's internal approval is recorded as the award decision it references under the single purpose 'Approval or award decision'.
cases.expect: Rejected: internal procurement approval is owned by the request; the award decision is a separate referenced record with its own purpose.

cases.input: A fixture is submitted with prose 'expect' and no expectedCode under requiresExpectedCode.
cases.expect: Rejected: every fixture carries a machine-checkable expectedCode.

cases.input: One artifact uses 'canonicalPublishable' while the reconciled hold text names 'publishableCanonical'.
cases.expect: Rejected: a single spelling of the publishability field is used across all EM-OPS-02 artifacts.
